description: ASUU withdrew its eight-month strike on 14 October 2022, describing the suspension as conditional. Millions of students had been at home since 14 February. The union's president appealed that future strikes 'should not go beyond two days'.
energy_note: Two hundred and forty days at home, mid-degree.

description: Students lost a cumulative four years to 16 ASUU strikes across 23 years, and undergraduates lost at least 13 months of academic calendar under one administration alone.
energy_note: Four years of a degree, spent waiting for it to resume.

aspect: The cost is borne by the student, not the parties
description: Rent continues, living costs continue, and the graduation date moves. Nobody involved in the dispute pays that.
money_note: Additional living costs across a strike period.
energy_note: Paying rent for a year that is not happening.

aspect: For women the delay has a different consequence
description: A degree that finishes at 26 instead of 22 collides with marriage pressure, and the commonest resolution is that the degree is abandoned rather than deferred.
energy_note: Four extra years, and the pressure does not wait.

aspect: And it feeds the credential problem
description: Educationists argue the interruptions are why graduates of Nigerian public universities are perceived as half-baked and why Nigerian certificates are not rated highly outside the country - which is EDU-003.
energy_note: The strike, and then the discount on the degree it produced.
